core: Definition of input devices (data flows into the computer) and output devices (data flows out to the user)
Common input devices: keyboard, mouse/trackpad, touchscreen, microphone, webcam, scanner, game controller
Common output devices: monitor/display, printer, speakers/headphones, projector
Devices that are both input and output: touchscreen, headset, network interface
The idea that the CPU processes what input captures and sends results to output devices
Ports and connections at a naming level: USB, HDMI, audio jack, Bluetooth/wireless
supporting: Peripheral as the general term for devices around the CPU and memory
Plug and Play / how peripherals are recognized
Accessibility framing: swapping input or output devices
outOfScope: Whole-system hardware overview (owned by Computer Hardware topic)
CPU, RAM, and storage internals (owned by CPU, RAM, and Storage topic)
Detailed electrical specifications, data rates, and protocol internals of each port standard

claims.claim: Input devices provide data and control signals into a computer; a keyboard, mouse, scanner, microphone, webcam, and game controller are input devices.
Output devices convert processed information into human-readable form; monitors, printers, speakers, headphones, and projectors are output devices.
Some devices are both input and output, including touchscreens, headsets, modems, and network interface controllers.

USB (Universal Serial Bus) is an expandable Plug and Play interface that provides a standard, low-cost connection for peripheral devices such as keyboards, mice, printers, scanners, and storage; the USB-IF maintains the standard.
Bluetooth is a short-range wireless standard operating in the 2.4 GHz band, used to connect peripherals such as keyboards, mice, speakers, and headphones, and is maintained by the Bluetooth SIG.
HDMI (High-Definition Multimedia Interface) carries digital video and audio over a single cable and connects displays to computers and consumer electronics.
Input and output devices are called peripherals because they surround the core CPU and memory of the computer.
